decisions.decision: Retain Liquid-500 for Salarium 1.0 portfolio construction; keep broad coverage as a separate discovery and research funnel.
decisions.finding: The broader point-in-time universe reduced drawdown in the risk-scaled policy, but materially weakened annualized return, Sharpe, and ranking IC. More names did not create a better portfolio model.
decisions.question: Did expanding the portfolio universe to roughly 2,000 names improve out-of-sample performance?
decisions.title: Keep the Liquid-500 portfolio universe

decisions.decision: Lock a 20-trading-day model horizon and 10-trading-day rebalance cadence.
decisions.finding: Separating prediction horizon from trading cadence showed that Salarium's signal is slower-moving. The 20D model traded every 10 days improved both return and Sharpe versus the original 5D/5D design.
decisions.question: Was the original five-day target and five-day rebalance cadence too short and too active?
decisions.title: Predict 20 days; rebalance every 10

decisions.decision: Keep Top-10 concentration with a rank-15 persistence buffer; manage joint risk through covariance rather than indiscriminate breadth.
decisions.finding: Additional breadth reduced volatility and turnover, but diluted return faster than it improved risk-adjusted performance. The model's useful alpha remained concentrated near the top of the ranking.
decisions.question: Could a broader 20–75 name portfolio preserve alpha while reducing risk?
decisions.title: Concentrate on the Top-10

decisions.decision: Use 60D shrinkage maximum diversification as the primary risk anchor; retain minimum variance as the defensive comparator.
decisions.finding: A 60D Ledoit-Wolf maximum-diversification portfolio improved Sharpe and Sortino while modestly improving drawdown versus inverse-volatility weighting. The optimizer completed without fallback in the selected configuration.
decisions.question: Could covariance-aware construction preserve concentrated alpha while reducing redundant correlated risk?
decisions.title: Replace standalone risk with joint risk

decisions.decision: Blend 25% signal-aware weights with 75% covariance-risk weights under the 18% single-name cap.
decisions.finding: A 25% signal blend increased the balanced mandate's simulated return while leaving overall Sharpe nearly unchanged. Higher blends continued to raise return but progressively increased volatility and drawdown.
decisions.question: Should conviction influence weights after Top-10 selection and covariance optimization?
decisions.title: Give the signal a governed 25% vote

decisions.decision: Retain a hard 1.25x governance ceiling as permission—not a target—and keep the selected mandate unlevered unless future risk evidence earns additional exposure.
decisions.finding: The selected portfolio and exposure policies did not require leverage above 1.00x in the committed evaluation. The risk layer found more value in de-risking than in borrowing additional capital.
decisions.question: Did the evidence justify using portfolio exposure above 1.00x?
decisions.title: Cap leverage; never force it
